hero.lead: A principality of 38,000 on the Mediterranean, where safe water, sanitation and power reach every home and lower-secondary completion is universal on the World Bank measure.

capital.heading: No public debt, and homes built by the State.

register.name: General primitive budget, 2026 (Law No. 1.586)
register.detail: Law No. 1.586 of 19 December 2025 · Journal de Monaco of 26 December 2025 · revenue €2,216.7M · expenditure ceiling €2,207.9M: €1,413.5M ordinary, €794.4M equipment and investment · revenue above the ceiling by €8.8M
register.note: A rectified budget for 2026 (bill No. 1.127, deposited 30 June 2026: revenue €2,144.7M, expenditure €2,138.9M) was withdrawn by the Government on 18 September 2026
register.text: The State budget of the Principality for 2026, voted by the Conseil National and promulgated on 19 December 2025, with revenue of €2,216.7 million against an expenditure ceiling of €2,207.9 million. Its €794.4 million of equipment and investment carries the State-built housing and the new hospital set out in its multi-year programme of works, serving the shelter and health standards.
by: Government of the Principality of Monaco

register.name: New Princess Grace Hospital Centre (Nouveau CHPG)
register.detail: Multi-year programme of works annexed to Law No. 1.586 · operation 709.997 · global credit €1,330.0M at 1 January 2026, up from €1,300.0M at 1 January 2025 · upgrading of the present CHPG (705.930/7) a further €164.7M
register.note: The global credit is the total authorised for the operation over its life, not the payment for 2026
register.text: The State’s programme to build a new Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace, the Principality’s public hospital, financed from the State budget. It serves the health standard, on which Monaco scores 85 on the WHO service coverage index.
by: Government of the Principality of Monaco

register.name: Le Bel Air State housing operation (197 apartments)
register.detail: Multi-year programme of works annexed to Law No. 1.586 · operation 705.917 · global credit €453.8M at 1 January 2026, up from €421.0M at 1 January 2025 · phase 2 of the National Housing Plan for Monegasques, with regular deliveries until 2029
register.note: The largest of the five operations of phase 2, presented by the Government on 6 June 2025
register.text: State-owned (domanial) apartments for Monegasque households, built and financed through the State budget under phase 2 of the National Housing Plan. It serves the shelter standard.
by: Government of the Principality of Monaco

register.name: Grand Ida State housing operation
register.detail: Multi-year programme of works annexed to Law No. 1.586 · operation 705.907 · global credit €426.1M at 1 January 2026, up from €420.0M at 1 January 2025
register.note: The global credit is the total authorised for the operation over its life, not the payment for 2026
register.text: State-owned apartments for Monegasque households in the Grand Ida operation, financed through the State budget. It serves the shelter standard.
by: Government of the Principality of Monaco

register.name: Fonds de Réserve Constitutionnel (Constitutional Reserve Fund)
register.detail: Article 41 of the Constitution · each budget surplus paid in, any excess of spending drawn from it · investment securities, equity securities, investment property and gold
register.note: Its 2025 self-assessment against the Santiago Principles (IFSWF) reports €2.3 billion of assets under management at the end of 2023, across 57 investment funds or mandates
register.text: The Principality’s reserve, held like a sovereign fund, into which each budget surplus is paid and from which any deficit is drawn; the Government states that Monaco is one of the very few countries in the world with no public debt. It underwrites the public finances as a whole rather than any one of the seven standards.
by: Government of the Principality of Monaco

register.name: National Housing Plan for Monegasques, phase 1
register.detail: Announced by the Sovereign Prince in 2019 · €1.5bn invested by the end of 2024 · 633 new State-owned housing units · 1,173 properties allocated to Monegasque households since 2019, as at 27 February 2025
register.note: Phase 2, from 2025: Héméra Block A (50 apartments), Bel Air (197), Larvotto Supérieur (35), La Luciole (27) and Hector Otto (76 to 90)
register.text: The first phase of the State’s plan to house Monegasque households in new State-owned homes, financed through the State budget. It serves the shelter standard.
by: Government of the Principality of Monaco

register.name: Fonds Vert National (National Green Fund), 2024
register.detail: Special Treasury Account · primitive budget 2024 · forecast spending €32.3M: nearly €16.4M for equipment or investment, €15.1M for subsidies and public interventions · topped up by €19.2M through the Transition Énergétique article
register.note: The rectified 2026 bill, later withdrawn, raised the fund’s revenue by €3.7M; no newer total was read at source
register.text: A special account of the State budget that finances sustainable development projects aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions and developing renewable energy. It serves the energy standard.
by: Government of the Principality of Monaco
